text: The chip in your phone holds billions of transistors. So what does a transistor actually do?
Zoom in. Way in. They're so small that hundreds fit across a single human hair.
A transistor is a tiny switch. Voltage on the gate lets current flow: a one. No voltage, no flow: a zero.
Wire four together and you get a logic gate. This one outputs zero only when both inputs are one.
Gates combine into circuits that add numbers, and memory cells that hold bits.
Billions of them sit in the silicon, and above them, more than ten layers of metal wiring connect them all.
A clock ticks billions of times a second, and on every tick, switches flip and signals move.
Billions of tiny switches, flipping billions of times a second. That's a chip.
